title: Three-Day Cough, Family Medicine
objectives: Document a chief complaint accurately from a lay description
Correctly document a pertinent negative without inventing unstated specifics

encounter.narrative: Patient reports a dry cough for the past three days. Denies fever. Denies chest pain. No shortness of breath. No recent travel.
encounter.hpi: Onset 3 days ago, non-productive, no clear trigger identified.
encounter.ros: Denies fever, denies chest pain, denies shortness of breath.
encounter.physicalExam: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. No respiratory distress.
encounter.assessment: Acute non-productive cough, likely viral upper respiratory infection.
encounter.plan: Supportive care, follow up if symptoms worsen or persist beyond 10 days.

requiredDocumentation.description: Document the chief complaint using clinical terminology
Document the cough as non-productive using clinical terminology
Document absence of shortness of breath using clinical terminology

commonErrors.description: Learner writes a specific temperature (e.g. 'Temp 37.0°C') though none was given in the encounter
Learner omits the pertinent negative for shortness of breath entirely
Learner writes 'throwing up' instead of converting to clinical terminology where applicable
